subject: Private inference rollback and evidence request
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@stratushealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-stratus@stratushealth.com
Date: 2028-09-11T09:12:00Z
Subject: Private inference rollout - rollback notice and impacted requests

Hi Hannah,

Wanted to notify you that during today's private deployment upgrade of the v0.9.2 -> v0.10.0 inference runtime (UTC 03:42–03:50), we observed a sustained latency surge (p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.8s) and a small fraction (~0.6%) of requests returned 500/connection resets for our inference endpoint used by triage pipelines. We initiated an automated rollback at 03:57 and traffic was routed to the previous version.

We captured request-level traces and a short set of error logs (attached: stratus_error_dump_20280911.log). The incident impacted a handful of high-priority workflows and we need a short timeline and any evidence you can share about the root cause (control plane connection state, agent handshake failures, or any known regression in the quantized kernel path).

Can you confirm whether Redwood rolled back on your side, what triggered the rollback, and share any diagnostic traces you captured? Also propose an ops window for a coordinated retry if you determine the release issue is resolved.

Thanks,
Sophie Turner
Director, Platform Engineering
StratusHealth

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-11T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Private inference rollout - rollback notice and impacted requests

Hi Sophie — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We're actively triaging from our side. Short answers up front: yes, the rollout was automatically rolled back by our canary controller after a spike in per-instance error rate; we have captured runtime traces and an agent-level diagnostic bundle and are attaching our preliminary dump (redwood_diagnostics_trace_20280911.zip).

Next steps we propose:
- We’ll run a quick correlation between your provided traces and our agent logs to identify handshake mismatches (target: 4 hours).
- Can we schedule a 30-minute bridge at 14:00 UTC today for a short calibration/handshake review? If that doesn't work for your ops window, propose alternatives.
- We will share a small set of evidence links (trace sampling, kernel metrics, and rollout decisions) within 2 hours.

Immediate ask from you: can you share the request IDs for two failing requests (so we can map them to our traces) and confirm whether you saw any control-plane TLS renegotiation messages in your side's logs?

I’ll loop Jordan Blake (ops) if we need to coordinate a targeted restart.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-11T10:01:00Z
Subject: Internal: quick triage notes and action items (do not forward)

Marcus/Jordan — summary from Sophie: Stratus ran our v0.10 rollout, saw latency p95 jumps and ~0.6% 500s, rolled back. They attached request traces.

Observed in our preliminary traces (attached):
- Short-lived control-plane heartbeat mismatches between orchestrator and private agents during the first 8 minutes of the rollout (03:43–03:51 UTC).
- One worker showed KV cache misalignment after a quantized kernel upgrade (inconsistent seq/kv pointers) leading to increased token-processing time for affected requests.
- Canary controller tripped on an error-rate threshold and initiated rollback at ~03:57.

Please action:
1) Marcus — prepare 2-page hypothesis doc with correlation between heartbeat errors and kernel load; include expected failure mode and whether this is deterministic or race-based (EOD UTC).
2) Jordan — assemble a minimal runbook to coordinate a targeted restart of the affected agent pool (safe rollback already completed). Include steps to capture golden traces pre/post restart and a suggested maintenance window.
3) Evelyn — coordinate SRE comms and prepare the short customer-facing summary we’ll send after the bridge.

I'll be on the bridge at 14:00 UTC to walk through the evidence.

Thanks,
Hannah

attachments: maintenance_window_proposal.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 12KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-11T14:40:00Z
Subject: Post-bridge summary: root cause hypothesis, rollback confirmation, and next steps

Hi Sophie — thanks again for joining the bridge. Below is a concise post-bridge summary and our immediate plan.

What happened (short):
- During the v0.10 canary rollout we observed a regression triggered by an interaction between the new quantized kernel path and our agent-side KV cache handling under concurrent warm-starts. In a subset of workers, KV pointer arithmetic produced an off-by-one that manifested as increased per-token compute time for affected requests. Simultaneously, transient control-plane heartbeat jitter caused the orchestrator to mark some agents unhealthy, increasing request fanout and amplifying latency on warm containers.

Action taken:
- Canary controller rolled back the release at ~03:57 UTC.
- We proactively drained and restarted the small cohort of agents that showed KV misalignment.
- We captured full traces (links below) and uploaded the diagnostic bundle (redwood_diagnostics_trace_20280911.zip).

Evidence we shared:
- Trace sample correlating a failing request id (stratus-rq-04127) to a worker-side cache pointer exception: https://drive.redwood.net/diagnostics/trace-20280911 (sampled traces)
- Raw diagnostic bundle: https://drive.redwood.net/diagnostics/trace-20280911/download
- HubSpot ticket for follow-up and rollback record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-7890

Planned next steps (coordination request):
1) We recommend a coordinated maintenance window to deploy a small fix that: disables the new quantized-hot-path on private agents, adds an assert to the KV pointer update, and re-runs the canary with tighter heartbeat thresholds. Estimated downtime: < 5 minutes per agent pool if drained properly. Proposed windows: 2028-09-14 02:00–04:00 UTC or 2028-09-14 22:00–00:00 UTC.
2) We will provide a short post-deploy verification script for you to run that captures golden traces and validates p95 latency.
3) We will share an audit bundle (control-plane heartbeat logs, canary decisions, and per-instance metrics) for your compliance records.

Immediate asks for Stratus:
- Confirm which of the two proposed windows you prefer.
- Provide two request IDs for deeper cross-correlation (you already shared one: stratus-rq-04127 — thanks).
- Confirm if you need us to provide any additional SOC2-aligned artifacts for your audit or procurement team.

We'll treat this as a Sev-2 and keep you updated hourly until the fix ships.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — helpful summary and appreciate the quick turnaround. We accept the 2028-09-14 22:00–00:00 UTC window (local DR team available).

Requests from our side before the window:
- Please upload the audit bundle (heartbeat logs + canary decisions) to the secure drive link and send the link via the HubSpot ticket.
- We need a short statement about data retention of the diagnostic bundle (how long Redwood will hold these traces) for our compliance team. Can you confirm retention and purge policy?

We'll provide two more request IDs by EOD our time and will run the verification script after the maintenance window.

Appreciate the coordination.

—
Sophie Turner
Director, Platform Engineering
StratusHealth
